facts.statement: The genus Wieslochia was first described by Gerald Mayr and Albrecht Manegold in 2006.
facts.quote: It was first described by Gerald Mayr and Albrecht Manegold in 2006.

facts.statement: Wieslochia lived in Germany during the early Oligocene, approximately 27.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Wieslochia is an extinct genus of passerine bird from the early Oligocene (27.8 million years ago) of Germany.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Wieslochia consists of a dissociated skeleton preserved on two slabs.
facts.quote: The holotype is a dissociated skeleton on two slabs.

facts.statement: A second specimen containing a mandible and a cranium was found in the same geological area as the holotype.
facts.quote: Another specimen consisting of a mandible and a cranium has been found in the same geological area.

facts.statement: A 2024 study suggests that Wieslochia and the related genus Crosnoornis belong to the Tyranni, likely as stem or crown group members of the Eurylaimides.
facts.quote: A 2024 study found strong support for it and the related Crosnoornis being members of the Tyranni, either as stem group or crown group members of the Eurylaimides.

facts.statement: Wieslochia is classified within the parent group Passeriformes.
The time range for Wieslochia is estimated to be between 33.9 and 27.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Rupelian to Rupelian (33.9 to 27.3 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Fossils of Wieslochia were discovered in a clay pit in Frauenweiler near Wiesloch, Germany.
rejected.quote: Remains of this genus have been found in a clay pit in Frauenweiler near Wiesloch, Germany.
